findings.finding: The table's fair value (546$) and the 'cheap by ~4%' row come from the DCF, whose terminal ROIC is an engine default (CONST, no evidence ids): 38.7% base, 45% bull, 27.1% bear (casefile company_path.scenarios.*.economics.engine_terminal_roic; fc driver_gaps terminal_roic). The analyst's own evidenced path uses ROIC 22% base / 14% bear / 31% bull, in line with the 3-year incremental ROIC of 22.5-23.6% (prefetch/forensic.json roic.incremental_roic; redteam detail incremental_roic_3y 0.225) while capex doubled. The two parts of one base story disagree by ~17 pp of ROIC: at the path's 22% the base value today is 489$ (economics.values year 0), i.e. the stock is ~7% ABOVE base value, not 4% below. The what_must_be_true capital_efficiency lever confirms it: the price holds only if growth needs at most 1.18x the base capital (terminal ROIC >= ~33%).
findings.where: companies/MSFT/out/casefile.json fc.driver_gaps[terminal_roic] and company_path.scenarios.{bear,base,bull}.economics (engine_terminal_roic vs roic); companies/MSFT/out/table_he.md rows 'שווי הוגן' and 'המחיר מול השווי'; position/path.json scenarios.*.economics.roic
findings.fix: Supply an evidenced terminal_roic per scenario in the driver spec (position/core.json drivers: base ~0.22-0.24 from the 3-year incremental ROIC, bear 0.14, bull 0.31, same evidence ids as position/path.json), rerun ticker-value so the DCF fair value and the path use one return on capital; if the DCF default is kept, show the 489$ path value next to 546$ and say the cheap/expensive sign depends on it.

findings.finding: Counter-thesis (pre-mortem, failed by late 2029): Microsoft's AI build-out turned out to be a bet on one customer. OpenAI is not only ~11% of revenue: by the FY2026 Q4 call, commercial RPO grew 84% to 678B but only 25% excluding OpenAI, which implies OpenAI held at least ~217B (about a third or more) of the backlog that the base converts at 30% a year; sequential RPO growth stopped (678B -> 677B). OpenAI, partly funded by Microsoft (12.0B of 13.0B funded, 7.2B receivable), could not finance its take-or-pay commitments; Azure growth fell to the teens, while 364.6B of not-yet-commenced datacenter leases, 169B of one-year purchase commitments and server depreciation (D&A 22.0B -> 34.3B in one year) were fixed. Operating margin went back to the FY2021-23 low-40s and below, FCF margin (already 20% in Q1 FY2027 vs ~31% in FY2024) compressed further, Microsoft used outside financing (management already said it may), and the market re-rated the stock from ~25x to the mid-teens as a capital-intensive utility. The key risk and the bear size OpenAI only by its revenue share; the backlog concentration is absent from the key risk, the bear events and the drivers. Early signals: RPO excluding OpenAI growth below 20% y/y; total commercial RPO flat or falling two quarters in a row; OpenAI receivable rising faster than OpenAI revenue; Azure growth below 35% before the H2 FY2027 capacity arrives; gross margin down more than 200 bp y/y; capex/OCF above 80%; any external debt raise for datacenters.
findings.where: position/core.json key_risk and scenario_events.bear; drivers.growth_anchor.reason (bear); gather/raw_documents/av_transcript_MSFT_2026Q4.json (passage 'RPO increased 25% when excluding OpenAI')
findings.fix: Register the FY2026 Q4 call statement as a fact (RPO +84% total vs +25% ex-OpenAI, all sequential growth from customers outside frontier model companies) and size the bear's OpenAI mechanism by its backlog share, not only its 10.8% revenue share; add it to the key_risk reading; add a falsifier on RPO excluding OpenAI.

findings.finding: Base capital efficiency is better than the latest year while capital intensity is still rising: base sales_to_capital 0.75 (three-year figure) vs 0.61 in FY2026 alone, with Q1 FY2027 cash capex 39.4B, Q2 guided above 50B and rising in H2, and 364.6B of leases not yet commenced (up from 329.1B a quarter earlier). The forensic ROIC (31%) and the incremental ROIC exclude operating leases, so both overstate returns on the capital actually committed. The base is thereby tilted favourable on the one lever the expectation gap says the price depends on (capital_efficiency required 1.18x).
findings.where: position/core.json drivers.sales_to_capital (base 0.75); prefetch/forensic.json roic; casefile what_must_be_true capital_efficiency
findings.fix: Set base sales_to_capital at or near the FY2026 0.61 unless evidence shows capex flattening inside FY2027, or state why the three-year figure is the better estimate; note that lease commitments are outside the ROIC capital base.

findings.finding: The bear's year-1 drop (-45% to 289$) is mostly a multiple call: 13.5-14.4x forward EPS, about 35% below the company's own 2022-2026 low (20.8x), from an ROIC of 14% that is below every year of its own record (31-38%, incremental 22.5%). The bear business change is real (margin 47% -> 38%, EPS flat FY2028-FY2031 at ~21$), but the 14% return is labelled unproven and rests partly on 'AI pricing falls', a bear event marked hypothesis (no evidence).
findings.where: position/path.json scenarios.bear (roic 0.14, justification unproven); casefile company_path.scenarios.bear.multiple_path; position/core.json drivers.mature_margin.bear reason and scenario_events.bear[3] (hypothesis)
findings.fix: Either evidence the 14% (e.g. a lease-inclusive incremental ROIC computation from the filings) or say next to the table that the bear price assumes a return on new capital below anything in the company's record and a multiple below its 5-year low; keep the pricing event labelled hypothesis.

findings.finding: Falsifier fx_bear_margin cannot refute the bear: 'FY2027 operating margin above 45%' is near-certain (Q1 FY2027 49.8%, Q2 guide ~46.8%) and the bear path itself has FY2027 at 47.1%; the bear's mechanism is a FY2028-FY2031 fall to 38%. Weak thresholds elsewhere: fx_bull_rpo triggers only if RPO falls below today's 677B, although the bull needs RPO to keep growing ~73%; fx_bear_openai uses the current 10B level, and rising OpenAI revenue does not refute an AI over-capacity bear.
findings.fix: fx_bear_margin -> FY2028 operating margin above 0.44 by 2028-08-15 (or gross margin not falling y/y in FY2028); fx_bull_rpo -> commercial RPO below ~750B by 2027-05-15; fx_bear_openai -> RPO excluding OpenAI growth above 0.25 y/y with Azure above 35% by 2027-08-15.

findings.finding: Base multiples 20.9x -> 19.3x sit at the own-history low (20.8x) while base EPS grows 13% then 12.5%; consistent with ROIC 22%, but it means the base year prices already embed a de-rating from today's ~25x forward, so the base 5-year +34% is mostly earnings growth. Worth one line so the base is not read as a conservative case.
findings.fix: State in scenarios_he.md that the base assumes a multiple near the 5-year low.

findings.finding: Shares are held flat at 7,426M in every scenario and year. Buybacks currently offset SBC (+1.2B net), but in the bear (FCF squeeze, possible outside financing) buybacks are the first cut while SBC (3.7% of revenue) continues, so bear EPS is slightly flattered.
findings.fix: Note it, or let bear share count grow by SBC net of a reduced buyback.

findings.finding: Gaps not carried into the bear or risks: own Taiwan/China supply share undisclosed (gather/macro.json gaps), 49% of revenue not split by country; Beneish unavailable (prefetch/forensic.json); Piotroski 6/9 with falling gross margin, asset turnover and current ratio, which the bear covers only through margin and sales_to_capital. The OpenAI equity stake (24-27% as-converted) is carried at book in investments: an asset at risk in the bear and an unvalued option in the bull, kept outside the base (correct) but not mentioned.
findings.where: gather/macro.json gaps; prefetch/forensic.json beneish, piotroski; casefile val.case.opening.marketable_investments
